what_its_for: Cefixime is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections, including ear infections, throat infections (such as strep throat), tonsillitis, bronchitis, urinary tract infections (UTIs), and some sexually transmitted infections like gonorrhea. It works by killing or stopping the growth of bacteria. It will NOT work for colds, flu, or other viral infections.
how_to_take: Take cefixime exactly as your doctor prescribed. You can take it with or without food. If it upsets your stomach, try taking it with a meal or a glass of milk. If you are taking the liquid suspension, shake the bottle well before each use and measure the dose carefully with the measuring spoon or oral syringe provided — do not use a regular kitchen spoon. Swallow tablets or capsules whole with a full glass of water. Finish ALL of your medicine even if you start feeling better, to make sure the infection is completely cleared.
dosing: The usual adult dose is 400 mg once a day, OR 200 mg twice a day (every 12 hours). For children, the dose is based on body weight and will be determined by your doctor. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions, as your dose may be different depending on the infection being treated.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Do NOT take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store cefixime tablets and capsules at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C and 25°C). Keep them away from heat, light, and moisture — do not store in the bathroom. For the liquid suspension, store it at room temperature or in the refrigerator (check your label). Throw away any unused liquid after 14 days. Keep all medications out of reach of children and pets.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking antacids that contain aluminum or magnesium at the same time as cefixime, as they may reduce how well the medication works — space them apart by at least 2 hours. Do not drink alcohol excessively while taking this antibiotic. Do not share your medication with others, even if they have similar symptoms. Avoid stopping your medication early just because you feel better.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor or seek medical help right away if you experience: a severe allergic reaction (rash, hives, swelling of the face, lips, tongue, or throat, difficulty breathing, or dizziness); severe or watery diarrhea that does not stop — this could be a serious bowel infection called C. difficile; severe stomach pain or cramps; yellowing of the skin or eyes (jaundice); dark urine; unusual bruising or bleeding; or if your infection does not seem to be getting better after a few days of treatment.
when_it_works: Most people start to feel better within 2 to 3 days of starting cefixime. However, it is very important to finish the entire course of antibiotics (usually 7 to 14 days, depending on your infection) even if you feel better sooner. Stopping early can allow the bacteria to come back and become harder to treat.
special_populations: PREGNANCY: Talk to your doctor before taking cefixime if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. It is generally considered relatively safe during pregnancy, but your doctor will weigh the benefits and risks. BREASTFEEDING: Small amounts of cefixime may pass into breast milk. Talk to your doctor before breastfeeding while on this medication. KIDNEY PROBLEMS: If you have kidney disease, your doctor may lower your dose. Make sure your doctor knows about any kidney problems before you start this medication. CHILDREN: Cefixime can be used in children, usually in liquid suspension form. The dose is based on the child's weight. ELDERLY: Older adults may need a lower dose if they have reduced kidney function. PENICILLIN ALLERGY: Tell your doctor if you are allergic to penicillin or any other antibiotics before taking cefixime, as there is a small chance of a cross-reaction.
